title: Injection is all you need: parallel universal logic in high-rate concatenated self-dual codes
authors: Joseph Sullivan, David Amaro, Michael A. Perlin
abstract: We propose a quantum architecture that achieves addressable and parallel universal fault-tolerant logical in high-rate codes. The codes are obtained from the flexible concatenation of small-distance high-rate self-dual CSS codes. Addressable and parallel universal logic on the resulting $K$ logical qubits is injected by fault-tolerantly preparing and then consuming diverse logical $K$-qubit CSS stabilizer states and logical $\lvert H \rangle^{\otimes K}$ global magic states. Flag-at-origin is used to prepare the stabilizer resource states while a concatenated cultivation protocol prepares the global magic states. These resource states are consumed by Steane-QEC or Knill-QEC teleportation gadgets, which simultaneously perform quantum error correction. Any quantum algorithm with $T$-depth $D_T$ can be executed by consuming $12D_T$ or fewer resource states. We benchmark the fault-tolerant preparation of the resource states for several two-level concatenations of the $[[k+4,k,2]]$ H codes and the Hamming $[[15,7,3]]$ code. In particular, we find that the concatenated cultivation offers at least one order of magnitude spacetime reduction compared to cultivation in the surface code.
summary: This paper details a novel architecture for achieving fault-tolerant, universal quantum computation by 'injecting' required logical gates rather than building them into the code structure. It leverages concatenated self-dual CSS codes and introduces efficient protocols like Flag-at-Origin and concatenated cultivation to manage resource state preparation. The work significantly advances the understanding of resource overheads for large-scale quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to achieve addressable and parallel universal fault-tolerant quantum logic using high-rate quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes, specifically overcoming the 'addressability problem.'
main_result: The authors propose an injection scheme using resource state consumption, demonstrating that any algorithm can be executed by consuming a polynomial number of resource states relative to its T-depth. They also show that concatenated cultivation offers significant spacetime reduction for magic state preparation.
method: The method involves decomposing quantum circuits into Clifford and T gate components, then implementing gates by fault-tolerantly preparing and consuming logical resource states (like $|	ext{H}angle^{\otimes k}$ and $|	ext{S}angle^{\otimes k}$) via specialized gadgets (Flag-at-Origin, Steane-QEC/Knill-QEC teleportation).
model_or_system: The system is based on quantum computation utilizing concatenated self-dual CSS codes, such as the H codes and Hamming codes, to encode logical qubits. The focus is on achieving fault tolerance for universal quantum computation.
key_observables: Resource state consumption ($\le 12D_T$ states for $D_T$-depth), logical error rate suppression ($O(p^{2\ell})$), and cost ratios (depth/qubit cost) comparing precompilation vs. other methods.
important_parameters: Concatenation level ($\ell$), physical error rate ($p$), and the number of logical qubits ($k$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the availability of global logical Hadamard ($	ext{H}^{\otimes k}$) and Phase ($	ext{S}^{\otimes k}$) gates (SWEL codes) to simplify the injection of Clifford gates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the injection architecture, showing how unitaries are compiled into Clifford and T layers, and how resource states are consumed. Tables provide quantitative comparisons of resource costs (depth, qubits) for different code types.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the necessity of resource states for Clifford gates (Theorem 1), extending this to universal computation via T-gate injection (Theorem 2), detailing resource state preparation protocols (Flag-at-Origin, concatenated cultivation), and finally analyzing the compilation and scheduling of circuits using sifting procedures.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly detailed, resource-aware blueprint for scaling fault-tolerant quantum computation, which is crucial for any theoretical physicist working on quantum computation or quantum information theory.
